name: Linde

header.one_liner: Contracted industrial gases with pass-through pricing; steady, and priced like it.
header.thesis: Linde compounds at 8% to 9% EPS growth with a record $8.1B contractual gas backlog. The engine's base case assumes a modest de-rating from 27.6x, which leaves the expected return below the hurdle. The disagreement is almost entirely about the exit multiple.

base.eps_label: FY2026 adjusted EPS, midpoint of company guidance $17.70 to $17.90
base.rev_label: FY2026E sales ($B), annualised from Q2 sales of $9.289B

rev_cagr.why: Q2 underlying sales rose 4% (2% price, 2% volume); reported sales rose 9% with currency and acquisitions. A record $8.1B sale-of-gas backlog and $11B project backlog support mid single digit growth.

margin_end.why: Net margin is about 22.3% on guided EPS. The base case adds roughly twenty basis points a year from productivity and mix. Adjusted operating margin was 29.5% in Q2, but the release says margin fell 60 basis points year on year, so expansion is not a given.

share_chg.why: Shareholder returns were $1,590M in Q2 including dividends; the split is not disclosed. The base case assumes a net buyback of about one percent a year.

exit_pe.why: Current multiple is 27.6x on guided EPS. The base case assumes a two-and-a-half point de-rating to 25x, against a 10-year yield near 5%. This is the number that decides the stance.

pillars.title: Contracts lock in volume and pass through energy
pillars.claim: Most gas is sold under long contracts with minimum purchase terms and energy cost pass-through, so profit grows even when volume is flat.

evidence.t: Q2 sales +9% but underlying +4%; 2% price, 2% volume
APAC margin down 120 bps but only 70 bps excluding cost pass-through

pillars.test: Does underlying sales growth stay at or above 3%?

pillars.title: Margin is flat to slightly down at the group
pillars.claim: Group operating margin was 60 basis points lower than a year ago in the quarter. Segment margins fell in all three regions.

evidence.t: Americas 31.2% (-50 bps), APAC 28.4% (-120 bps), EMEA 35.7% (-40 bps)

pillars.test: Does adjusted operating margin stop falling in Q3?

pillars.title: Capital intensity is rising
pillars.claim: FY2026 capex is guided to $5.5B to $6.0B; Q2 free cash flow was $833M on $2,271M operating cash flow. Growth is being funded by investment.
pillars.test: Does return on capital hold above 23% as capex rises?

pillars.title: Engineering backlog is a lead indicator
pillars.claim: Third-party equipment backlog of $3.0B and order intake of $871M show project demand, but engineering margin is only 16%.
pillars.test: Does order intake stay above $800M a quarter?

variant.street: Premium multiple for the most defensive industrial: low volatility, contracted cash flows, and a record backlog.
variant.ours: The business case is intact. The return case is weak because the price already pays a staple-like multiple while Treasuries yield about 5%; the engine needs a 28x exit to reach the hurdle.
variant.could_be_wrong: If long rates fall and defensive compounders re-rate, a 28x multiple is plausible and this becomes a positive stance.
variant.would_change_mind: Underlying volume above 3% for two quarters, or the price falling toward 22x guided EPS.

moat.summary: Local density, long contracts and pass-through pricing; the duopoly-style structure makes margin defensible.
moat.detail: Existing Porter card (FY2025 10-K) rates Linde Strong.

quality.leverage_note: Net debt not retrieved from the release (not stated).

catalysts.label: Linde Q3 2026 earnings and conference call
catalysts.note: Guide: Q3 adjusted EPS $4.45 to $4.55 (+6% to +8%); FY $17.70 to $17.90.

tripwires.text: Q3 adjusted EPS below $4.45 (bottom of guide)

risks: Industrial and chemical volume weakness in EMEA (volume was lower in Q2).
Project execution on large on-site plants.
Rising capex diluting free cash flow.

lenses.eisman: Segment margins fell in all three regions; ask whether pass-through is hiding real cost pressure.
lenses.munger: A great business bought at 27x earnings is still an average investment if rates stay here.
lenses.buffett: Exactly his kind of franchise; the question is only the price.
lenses.hohn: Durable, contracted, pricing power: the cleanest profile of the four, the question is the 8.1B backlog conversion.

sources.title: Linde plc Form 8-K, Q2 2026 earnings release
Financial Modeling Prep: company profile, treasury rates, market risk premium

gaps: Net debt, dividends and buybacks not stated in the release.
FY2026 reported sales not stated; annualised from Q2.

review.basis: Q2 2026 10-Q and release. Q3 reports on 29 October; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: The best operator in a three-player oligopoly. The business is not the debate; the 20% premium to gas peers is.
review.model: Linde sells industrial gases (oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, specialty gases) under long contracts, and builds the plants that make them.

how_it_earns.v: Plant built next to a customer, 15 to 20 year take-or-pay contract, energy costs passed through.
Liquid gas trucked locally. Density of plants and routes sets the cost advantage.
Cylinders to small users. Highest price per unit, most local.
Designs and builds plants for Linde and third parties. Lumpy, low margin, early signal of demand.

mix.note: Segment profit is Linde's own measure, excluding Linde AG merger purchase accounting. EBITDA adds back segment depreciation.

rows.label: Americas
rows.driver: US electronics and manufacturing volumes, 2% pricing

rows.label: EMEA
rows.driver: Price and productivity offset falling manufacturing volume

rows.label: APAC
rows.driver: New plants starting up, electronics and chemicals

rows.label: Engineering
rows.driver: Project timing; $3.0B third-party backlog, $871M Q2 orders

rows.label: Other
rows.driver: LAMT coatings and global helium wholesale

review.position: One of three global gas majors with Air Liquide and Air Products, and the largest by sales. Local density makes each regional market close to a duopoly.

sources: Switching cost of an on-site plant
moat.threat: Moat is safe. The return on new capital is what can slip.

what_numbers_say.t: Growth is half price, half volume
what_numbers_say.d: Underlying sales +4% in Q2: price +2%, volume +2%. Reported +9% adds currency, acquisitions and pass-through, which carry little profit.
Adjusted operating margin 29.5% vs 30.1%. Cost inflation outran pricing in every region; EMEA held up only after stripping pass-through.

what_numbers_say.t: Capex is rising to fund the backlog
what_numbers_say.d: H1 capex $2.78B against $4.51B operating cash flow. Full-year capex guide $5.5B to $6.0B for an $8.1B sale-of-gas backlog.

what_numbers_say.t: Returns to shareholders exceed free cash flow
what_numbers_say.d: H1 buybacks $1.66B plus dividends $1.48B against free cash flow of $1.73B; net new debt of $1.65B filled the gap.

balance.read: Leverage is modest and the rating is protected, but buybacks are now partly debt-funded.
facts: $5.0B and $1.5B undrawn credit lines, no covenants
Management commits to strong Moody's and S&P ratings

flags.flag: Adjusted EPS excludes merger accounting, eight years on
flags.evidence: Linde AG purchase accounting adds $0.35 to Q2 adjusted EPS of $4.50 (8%). GAAP EPS was $4.15.

flags.flag: Return on capital is quoted on the adjusted base
flags.evidence: Company quotes 23.5% return on capital. On reported equity and debt, ROIC is about 12% because the merger goodwill stays in the base.
Cost pass-through added 1% to Q2 sales with minimal profit. Margin comparisons should use underlying sales.

forecast_basis.rev_cagr: Driver-based: price plus volume plus backlog start-ups, cross-checked with guidance
forecast_basis.margin_end: Judgment: assumes productivity offsets inflation; Q2 shows it did not
forecast_basis.share_chg: Below trend: buybacks ran -2.2% a year; base assumes -1% as capex rises
forecast_basis.exit_pe: Judgment: modest de-rating with 10-year yields near 5%

base.story: Price and start-ups carry 4% to 5% underlying growth, EPS compounds 8% to 9%, the multiple drifts lower.
base.needs: Pricing at or above inflation; backlog starts on time

downside.story: Industrial recession: volumes fall in EMEA and the Americas, price fades, the premium multiple compresses.
downside.needs: Underlying growth below 2% for two quarters

upside.story: Electronics fabs and clean-energy plants start up together; EPS growth reaches double digits and the multiple holds.
upside.needs: Backlog conversion plus volume recovery in EMEA

risks.how: Manufacturing and chemicals customers cut output, so merchant and packaged volumes fall. EMEA volume is already -1%.
Chip fabs are the main source of new on-site contracts. Delays push out start-ups and shrink the backlog.

risks.cause: Pricing power fades as inflation cools
risks.how: Linde's price gains track inflation. If price falls below cost inflation, margin compresses, as it did by 60 bps in Q2.

risks.cause: New capital earns less than old
risks.how: Capex is near 16% of sales. If new plants earn less than the 23.5% company return on capital, growth dilutes returns.
A staple-like multiple competes with a 5% Treasury yield. Higher-for-longer rates lower what investors pay for steady growth.

peer_read.why_premium: Linde earns more on capital than Air Liquide and Air Products, has delivered 12 straight earnings beats, and has avoided the large project write-downs that hit Air Products.
peer_read.why_not: Air Products' normalised EBITDA margin is higher, and Air Liquide trades at a lower multiple on similar consensus growth. The premium rests on execution, not structural superiority.
peer_read.peers_note: Air Liquide reports half-yearly, so its trailing figures are the last full fiscal year.

questions: Is buyback spending above free cash flow a sign of confidence or of a mature business?
Should the eight-year-old merger adjustment still be excluded from EPS?
Does the 23.5% return on capital hold on new electronics contracts?
